ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A circular coil with a radius of \( r = 10\,\mathrm{cm} \) and 100 turns rotates uniformly in a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic induction strength of \( B = \frac{5}{\pi^{2}} \) T. The coil rotates around the central axis \( O O^{\prime} \), which is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field, at a speed of \( n = 600\,\mathrm{r/min} \). Timing begins when the coil reaches the neutral plane position.

1. What is the instantaneous value expression of the induced electromotive force generated in the coil?
2. What is the instantaneous value of the induced electromotive force in the coil at $t=\frac{1}{60}$ s?
3. What is the average value of the induced electromotive force generated by the coil from $t=0$ to $t=\frac{1}{60}$ s?

The coil rotates around the central axis \( O O^{\prime} \), which is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field, at a speed of \( n = 600\,\mathrm{r/min} \). Timing begins when the coil reaches the neutral plane position. 1. What is the instantaneous value expression of the induced electromotive force generated in the coil? 2. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circular coil, with a vertical dashed axis OO′ in the center passing through the center of the coil; around and inside the coil, multiple “×” symbols indicate that the direction of the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward; above the axis there is a curved arrow, indicating that the coil rotates around the OO′ axis. This rotating axis is located in the plane of the coil in the figure, and is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field. Then reason: The problem gives N=100, r=10 cm=0.10 m, B=5/π² T, rotational speed n=600 r/min=10 r/s, so the angular velocity ω=2πn=20π rad/s. The coil area S=πr²=π(0.10)²=0.01π m². Timing starts from the neutral plane; according to the method, take the magnetic flux Φ=NBS cos(ωt), therefore the induced electromotive force e=-dΦ/dt=NBSω sin(ωt). The amplitude is NBSω=100×(5/π²)×(0.01π)×20π=100 V, so e=100 sin(20πt) V. When t=1/60 s, the phase 20πt=20π/60=π/3, therefore e=100 sin(π/3)=50√3 V. The average value from 0 to 1/60 s is: ē=(1/(1/60))∫_0^{1/60}100 sin(20πt)dt=60×[100/(20π)(1-cos(π/3))]=60×(5/π)×(1/2)=150/π V.
